neighbours.label: the adjective 'perfect' (and 'better'): an ideal or flawless degree, as opposed to plain good/bad on the - pole
fire: The sauce had a perfect balance of salt and acid.
That sentence uses the present perfect form of the verb.
Saturday was a perfect afternoon for sailing.
Her new bike is better than the one she sold.
The lens forms a perfect circle of light on the wall.
In my perfect world, every train would run on time.
He found the perfect spot for the tent by the lake.
Practice makes the second draft better than the first.
quiet: The sauce had a nice balance of salt and acid.
That sentence uses the past form of the verb.
Saturday was a sunny afternoon for sailing.
Her new bike is lighter than the one she sold.
The lens forms a small circle of light on the wall.
In my ideal town, every train would run on time.
He found a quiet spot for the tent by the lake.
Practice makes the second draft shorter than the first.
